The effectiveness of patient control analgesia in the treatment of acute traumatic pain in the emergency department: a randomized controlled trial.

CONCLUSION: PCA provides more effective pain relief and patient satisfaction when compared with the conventional method of bolus intravenous injection for the relief of traumatic pain in the emergency department setting.

I don't think anybody doubts that PCA is more effective than IV push, all else being equal. I think the biggest barrier to more widespread use is the cost.

The pumps themselves cost on the order of $4000 to $5000 each, and even if we used them only on traumas we'd need at least five or six of them. If we used them routinely to replace IVP analgesia, we'd need over twenty. I'm sure my manager can think of more critical places to spend a hundred grand.

More importantly, it takes significant staff time to hook up and configure each PCA and educate the patient in how to properly use it. This would often be wasted effort in the ED. You don't know what each patient's analgesia requirements are, and some people would be fine with oral meds, perhaps after a single IV dose to "take the edge off." You don't know which patients will be admitted, and many people would get pain medication only for a few hours and then be discharged to home, which means the PCA would be overkill.

Further, the drug container for a PCA is much larger than a single IVP vial, and so would involve larger amounts of drug wastage. That's another big money sink.

Considering that PCA use in the study only lowered patients' self-reported pain score by about a point (from 5.9 to 4.8), I don't think most ED teams would deem it worth the significant cost and hassle.

Maybe but in my EDs it is not uncommon to have admits held for 24+ hours. These would seem like great candidates for PCA. Also you have to add up all the time for the RN to deal with orders, Pyxis, drawing meds, slow push etc. I would think it would be a time saver in many cases.

Hold patients are a different issue. Once you have an admit order, that's no longer an emergency patient nor managed by the ED physician, even if they continue physically occupying an ED bed. That is now an inpatient and they're managed by the admitting physician, under inpatient policies and procedures. So, any change to "treatment of acute pain in the emergency department" doesn't apply anymore anyway.

What time of day are your ketones the highest?

I think it varies from person to person. If you exercise heavily, especially when fasted, your ketones will likely be highest shortly after that period. I would think that they would be highest in the morning, before you eat. But, I have also read about people who say their ketones rise during the day. Who knows?

If you're going to track ketones, the best idea would be to pick a specific time during the day and test each day at that time. I always preferred first thing in the morning, as that tends to be the most controlled time of the day for me (no food, water, exercise to change the results).

I don't have the money (or inclination) to buy more test strips these days and do an hour-by-hour test over several days to get an n=1 for highest time of day. Plus, my fingers would hate me by the end of that period. LOL

Display loading time and percentage on the loading screen

During some old PvP livestream that I can't really remember, a dev told everyone how to display a percentage when loading. This blogpost is 1-2 years old. If it doesn't work, use the link below.

There's also this link with other types of command lines that you might find useful. Also how to use the command lines on Linux and Mac.

If you can't click the link:

  1. Navigate to your Guild Wars 2 folder in your documents (C:\Users\YOURNAME\Documents\Guild Wars 2).
  2. Right click on Gw2.exe, and click “create shortcut”.

(Optional) Place the new shortcut on your desktop for easy access.

 Now to add the required parameter to show loading times, simply do the following:

  1. Right click on your newly-made (or already existing) Guild Wars 2 shortcut and click on “properties“.

  2. A window will pop up. Click on the tab called “Shortcut”

  3. Inside the box labeled “Target“, after you see “C:\Users\YOURNAME\Documents\Guild Wars 2\Gw2.exe”, add a space (outside of the quotation marks) and type in -mapLoadInfo. Your “target” box should now look like this:

    “C:\Users\YOURNAME\Documents\Guild Wars 2\Gw2.exe” -mapLoadInfo

  4. Click “apply” and “ok“, then run your game!
